items.stem: What are elastomers? Give an example and a feature of their stress-strain curve.
items.answer: Substances like rubber or the aorta tissue that can be stretched to large strains; the curve has no well-defined linear region.

items.answer: A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Distinguish between ductile and brittle materials using the stress-strain curve.
items.answer: Ductile materials (copper) have a large gap between elastic limit and fracture; brittle materials (glass) fracture soon after the elastic limit.

items.stem: Steel is said to be more elastic than rubber. Explain.
items.answer: For the same stress steel has a much smaller strain, so its Young's modulus (and restoring tendency) is much larger.
items.markingKey: Y = stress/strain (1 mark); steel has larger Y (1 mark).

A light rod of length 1.2 m is supported at its ends by two wires of equal length, steel (A) and aluminium (B). The cross-sectional area of A is 3 times that of B. At what distance from A should a mass be hung to produce (i) equal stresses and (ii) equal strains in the two wires? (Y_steel = 2.0 × 10¹¹ N m⁻², Y_Al = 7.0 × 10¹⁰ N m⁻²)
items.answer: (i) 0.300 m from A (ii) 0.125 m from A
items.markingKey: Let x from A. Moments: T_A x = T_B (L − x) (1). (i) equal stress ⇒ T_A/T_B = A_A/A_B = 3 ⇒ x = L/(1 + 3) = 0.300 m (2). (ii) equal strain ⇒ T_A/T_B = (A_A Y_A)/(A_B Y_B) = 8.571 ⇒ x = 0.125 m (2).

items.stem: Two wires of the same material, one twice as thick as the other, carry the same load. Compare their extensions if their lengths are equal.

items.stem: Why are crane ropes made of a number of thin wires braided together rather than one thick wire?
items.answer: They have the same strength but are flexible and easier to handle; damage to one wire does not cause failure.

Rock at the base of a mountain begins to flow when the stress exceeds about 3.2 × 10⁸ N m⁻². If the density of rock is 2700 kg m⁻³, estimate the maximum height of a mountain on Earth. Why could mountains on Mars (g ≈ 3.7 m s⁻²) be taller? (g = 9.8 m s⁻²)
items.answer: About 12 km; on Mars smaller g means a taller column for the same stress
items.markingKey: Stress at base = hρg (1); hρg ≤ σ ⇒ h = σ/(ρg) = 3.2 × 10⁸/(2700 × 9.8) = 12100 m ≈ 12 km (1); h ∝ 1/g, so mountains on Mars can be about 2.6 times taller (Olympus Mons ≈ 22 km) (1).

items.stem: The linear part of the stress-strain graph of a copper wire passes through the origin and the point (strain 9.1 × 10⁻⁴, stress 1 × 10⁸ N m⁻²). The yield strength is about 2.5 × 10⁸ N m⁻². items.answer: (i) 1.1 × 10¹¹ N m⁻² (ii) 0.0011 (iii) the wire is permanently deformed (plastic region)
